newsitem.title: UK: British manufacturing output falls in November.
newsitem.headline: British manufacturing output falls in November.

text.p: British manufacturing output fell by 0.5 percent in November after a rise of 0.5 percent in October, the Office for National Statistics said on Friday.
Treasury minister Angela Knight said however that the underlying trend in manufacturing and industrial output was upwards.
Manufacturing output rose by 0.2 percent in the year to November after a 0.5 percent rise in the year to October.

Industrial production rose by 0.4 percent in November after having been unchanged the previous month. The November year-on-year rise was 1.3 percent, compared with a rise of 1.4 percent in the year to October.

Analyst Philip Shaw of Union Plc called the figures "very surprising", adding: "It may well be that the appreciation in sterling is having an impact on manufacturing output much earlier than most of had been expecting.
Knight said prospects for manufacturing industry in 1997 were good. "Monthly figures can be erratic," she said.
